disclaimer: Each case sets what the law promised against what was done afterwards, using the official text on both sides. The page does not claim the tax caused any indicator to worsen: it holds to account the promise made by whoever asked for the money. Cases not yet checked against the original document do not appear.

cases[1].loophole.name: A new law, not a breach
cases[1].loophole.explanation: No rule was violated. Congress passed a law that added five areas to the original list and widened a sixth to include public disasters. It is the same mechanism as the CPMF, fifteen years later and under a different government: the promise was not broken outside the law, it was rewritten inside it.

cases[2].loophole.name: Five rewrites, three governments
cases[2].loophole.explanation: The rule was never breached: it was amended. Amendments 113 and 114, in 2021, changed how court-ordered debts are counted; 123, in 2022, put benefits outside the ceiling in an election year; 126, at the end of 2022, opened room for the transition of government; and Complementary Law 200, in 2023, replaced the whole regime. Different governments, different parties, the same mechanism.
cases[2].question: A rule written into the Constitution to last twenty years was rewritten five times in seven. How long does a fiscal promise last in Brazil?

cases[3].collected.lastYear: and 50% of research spending as a credit for industry, in the same law
cases[3].collected.note: Both measures are in the same statute, signed on the same day.
cases[3].loophole.name: The tax rode in on a law about something else
cases[3].loophole.explanation: The statute's summary mentions neither e-commerce nor consumer imports: it creates a mobility and innovation programme for the car industry. Taxing small parcels appears as an amendment to a 1980 decree-law, in the same text that grants industry a credit for half of what it spends on research and development.

cases[2].tribute.name: New Fiscal Regime, the spending ceiling
cases[0].end.text: On 19 September 2007, the day the Chamber began voting on the extension, President Lula said in a speech: "Nenhum governo, nem do PT, nem do PMDB, nem do PSDB, nem do PFL, se viessem mais partidos novos, ninguém conseguiria governar sem a CPMF." And he suggested that anyone wanting to discuss ending it should propose it "for after 2010". Eighty-five days later, on 13 December, the Senate voted the extension down, and the contribution died on 31 December 2007. Lula himself governed three more years without it, then Dilma, Temer, Bolsonaro and Lula again. Federal revenue went from R$ 618bn in 2007 to R$ 826.5bn in 2010.
cases[3].outcome.indicator: The law that gives industry half its research back is the same one that started taxing a 50-dollar purchase
cases[3].outcome.split[0].destino: was what anyone buying up to US$ 50 from a foreign site began paying in import duty, from August 2024
cases[3].outcome.split[1].destino: is how much industry can write off its research and development spending, returned as a financial credit — in the same law, signed the same day
cases[3].collected.amount: 20% on purchases up to US$ 50, from August 2024 to May 2026
cases[3].end.text: The tax lasted twenty-one months. Since 12 May 2026 the federal import duty on purchases up to US$ 50 is ZERO on Remessa Conforme platforms — only the state VAT remains. The 50% research credit for industry is still standing.
cases[3].end.source: Federal Revenue Service — New Rules, table in force since 12/05/2026
cases[3].question: The same law gave industry back half of what it spends on research and charged 20% from someone buying 50 dollars' worth. The charge ended in 2026; the industry credit did not. Which of the two was called protecting national commerce?
cases[0].loophole.name: The harshest indictment came from the foundation of the president who created it
cases[0].loophole.explanation: The timeline published by the Fundação FHC records what happened to the health money: "Created at a time when the public health system faced a severe budget squeeze, the CPMF ended up becoming a substitute contribution, and its revenue merely took the place of previous budget revenue. The more money the tax collected, the less the Treasury itself invested in health — which resulted in little change to the funding of the health system." The health minister who backed the contribution, Adib Jatene, left office in November 1996.
cases[0].end.source: O Estado de São Paulo, 20/09/2007, p. A5 and 16/12/2007, p. A4 — clippings from the Senate's BDSF archive; Federal Revenue Service historical series
